conclusions: Only a new-conversation project with a defaults error or its pending explicit retry renders the new button. Clicking calls defaults.refresh() directly; no catalog sync, provider write, mutation operation ID, model call or task submission is added.

The local retryingDefaults flag keeps the read-in-progress button visible while useResource clears the error; defaults.loading disables the control and its callback also rejects a second click. Failure restores a usable retry; success hides it.
No draft, attachment, provider, model, effort or permission state is modified by retry. Existing useResource request-key/generation/AbortController handling continues to discard obsolete results.
Existing composer loading, connection, runtime unknown, history and operation guards remain unchanged. A successful settings read cannot acknowledge uncertain activity or make it sendable.

The added regression verifies normal send admission before retry with valid explicit settings, one read despite a busy click, retry failure then success, exact unchanged draft/model/provider/effort, readiness remaining blocked under unknown and becoming enabled only after a known state. Exact post-click request equality proves only the two user-requested defaults/read calls and no operationId.
Existing tests and assertions are preserved; no retry loops, sleeps, timeout increases, skipped tests or production-capacity relaxation are introduced.

originalObservationBoundary.confirmedSource: Runtime service deliberately permits only one uncached effective-defaults probe. useResource stores an error until key or explicit refresh changes; previous model-directory refresh and project switching already provided indirect recovery.
originalObservationBoundary.rootLiveObservation: Root reported that selecting the new project and returning to the original project restored defaults and that sendEnabled=true with an unsent test draft. This reviewer did not perform browser interaction or commercial inference.
originalObservationBoundary.classification: Explicitly authorized UX recovery improvement. Not evidence of a permanently stuck runtime, universally blocked text sending, or a reproduced exact pair of initial concurrent requests.
